findings: An infiltrative pancreatic cancer measuring 63 mm is observed in the body of the pancreas. Serosal invasion and retropancreatic tissue invasion are noted. There is contact of more than 180° with the superior mesenteric vein, suggesting invasion. No invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum is observed. Contact of less than 180° with the celiac artery is noted, raising suspicion of invasion, although no deformation or stenosis of the celiac artery is observed. Additionally, there is contact of more than 180° with the splenic artery, suggesting invasion. The tumor does not involve the common hepatic artery or the proper hepatic artery. No other local invasion factors are identified. Lymph node metastasis is observed in one node at station 10. No other metastases are observed.

responses.content:
Task 1: Diagnose the local invasion factors of pancreatic cancer.

CH0 (no contact with common hepatic artery)
DU0 (no invasion beyond the inferior border of the duodenum)
S1 (serosal invasion)
RP1 (retropancreatic tissue invasion)
PV1 (invasion of superior mesenteric vein)
A1 (contact with celiac artery, raising suspicion of invasion)
PL0 (no contact with proper hepatic artery)
OO0 (no other local invasion factors)

Task 2: Determine the classification for local invasion (T classification) of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the size of the tumor (63 mm), it is classified as T3.

Task 3: Determine the N classification of pancreatic cancer.

Regional lymph nodes for pancreatic cancer in the body of the pancreas are:
- Station 10 (left gastric artery)
- Station 11 (common hepatic artery)
- Station 12 (proper hepatic artery)
- Station 13 (left gastric artery, common hepatic artery, proper hepatic artery)
- Station 10 is the only metastatic lymph node station in the regional stations.
There is 1 metastatic lymph node in the regional stations.

N classification: N1a (1 metastatic lymph node in the regional stations)

Task 4: Determine the M classification of pancreatic cancer.

No distant metastases are observed. The M classification is M0.

Task 5: Determine the resectability classification of pancreatic cancer.

Based on the results of Task 1 and Task 4, the tumor is resectable because there are no distant or non-regional metastases.

Resectability classification: R (Resectable)

Task 6: Determine the overall stage according to the JPS staging system.

T classification: T3
N classification: N1a
M classification: M0

Stage classification: Stage IIA
